longevity.headline: Physical activity is linked to delayed ovarian aging in mice and human cohort data
longevity.summary: Because the full abstract was unavailable, this summary is based on the published title and linked discussion. In an analysis of 152,435 UK Biobank participants alongside mouse experiments, higher physical activity was associated with delayed ovarian aging and extended reproductive lifespan. Mechanistic experiments in mice suggested this effect operates partly through adiponectin signaling, as knocking out adiponectin eliminated the protective benefit, while an adiponectin receptor agonist mimicked it. The human data are observational, meaning they show an association rather than proven causation, and animal mechanistic findings may not fully translate to humans. Practical meaning: Regular physical activity may support reproductive longevity, but clinical implications for human ovarian aging remain under investigation.
longevity.evidenceNote: Observational cohort of 152,435 participants and mouse mechanistic studies · summary based on tweet discussion only (no abstract)

primaryLinks.title: Physical activity delays ovarian aging in part through adiponectin-related signaling pathways

longevity.headline: Lower Plasma Selenium Linked to Higher All-Cause and Cancer Mortality in Older Adults
longevity.summary: In a 9-year prospective cohort study of 1,389 older adults (aged 59–71 at baseline) from the French EVA study, researchers evaluated the association between baseline plasma selenium levels and mortality. Over the follow-up period, 101 participants died. Average baseline plasma selenium was slightly higher in survivors (1.10 µmol/L) compared to those who died (1.01 µmol/L). After adjusting for sociodemographic, dietary, health, and cognitive variables, each 0.2 µmol/L decrease in plasma selenium was associated with a 54% higher risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.25–1.88) and a 79% higher risk of cancer mortality (adjusted RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32–2.44). A key limitation is the observational design, which cannot establish causation or rule out residual confounding, such as underlying illness driving lower nutrient levels. Practical meaning: Adequate dietary selenium intake may support long-term health in older age, but it is unclear whether supplementation improves longevity.
longevity.evidenceNote: Prospective cohort study of 1,389 older adults · summary based on the abstract

primaryLinks.title: Selenium and mortality in the elderly: results from the EVA study.

longevity.headline: Plasma Proteomic Panel Distinguishes Major Types of Neurodegenerative Dementia
longevity.summary: In a multicenter study analyzing 1,318 discovery plasma samples and 805 independent validation samples across international cohorts, researchers evaluated whether blood proteomics could differentiate Alzheimer's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Distinct protein signatures emerged: glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) rose along the Alzheimer's continuum, integrins alpha-V and alpha-M decreased in DLB, and elevated neurofilament light chain (NfL) with lower GFAP was associated with FTD. A condensed 21-protein panel achieved an external validation area under the curve of approximately 0.85 for differential diagnosis across conditions. Because this was a retrospective biomarker analysis, these findings reflect statistical associations rather than established disease mechanisms. The main limitation is that the panel was evaluated in specialized research cohorts and requires prospective testing in unselected clinical populations with mixed pathologies. Practical meaning: Multiplex blood protein panels may eventually assist clinicians in distinguishing between different dementia subtypes, but the test remains a research tool not yet ready for routine practice.
longevity.evidenceNote: Multicenter biomarker discovery and validation study of 2,123 plasma samples · summary based on the abstract

primaryLinks.title: Plasma proteome profiling identified biomarkers for the differential diagnosis and molecular staging of neurodegenerative dementias

longevity.headline: Critical Review Challenges Role of Sirtuins as Conserved Longevity Genes
longevity.summary: A critical review evaluated decades of preclinical research on sirtuins (such as yeast SIR2 and animal homologs) to assess whether they act as conserved longevity regulators. The analysis argues that early lifespan-extension findings in model organisms often reflected experimental artifacts and confirmation bias, noting that sirtuin activation does not consistently extend life and can accelerate aging under certain metabolic conditions. The author concludes that sirtuins lack a reliable, conserved connection to animal lifespan and are unlikely to be the primary mediators of NAD+ repletion. A key limitation is that this is a narrative critique synthesizing historical model-organism data rather than new experimental or human clinical trial evidence. Practical meaning: It is unclear whether targeting sirtuins provides any lifespan or healthspan benefits in humans.
longevity.evidenceNote: Critical review of preclinical studies · summary based on the abstract

primaryLinks.title: Sirtuins are not conserved longevity genes

longevity.headline: Blood metabolites linked to midlife cognitive performance and brain MRI measures
longevity.summary: In a cohort study of 1,082 dementia-free middle-aged adults from the Rotterdam Study (with findings replicated in independent cohorts), researchers examined the relationship between 991 blood metabolites, cognitive performance, and brain MRI measures. Fourteen metabolites were replicated for associations with cognition, with the dietary antioxidant ergothioneine showing the strongest link and mirroring signatures seen in incident Alzheimer's disease. Lifestyle, clinical variables, and medications explained up to 28.6% of metabolite variance; notably, antacid use was linked to lower cognitive scores, with lower ergothioneine levels statistically mediating 31.5% of this association. A key limitation is the observational design, meaning these findings demonstrate associations rather than direct causation. Practical meaning: Blood metabolites such as ergothioneine may reflect early neurological health, but it is unclear whether supplementing or altering these levels directly influences long-term dementia risk.
longevity.evidenceNote: Cohort study of 1,082 middle-aged adults with replication cohorts · summary based on the abstract

primaryLinks.title: The blood metabolome of brain health in midlife and influences of genes, microbiome and exposome

longevity.headline: Metabolically Healthy Obesity Linked to Elevated Cardiovascular and Mortality Risks
longevity.summary: In a prospective cohort study of 157,159 UK Biobank participants (mean age 56.5 years, 55.6% women) followed for a median of 12.9 years, researchers evaluated outcomes in individuals with obesity without baseline metabolic abnormalities (hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidaemia) compared to normal-weight individuals without abnormalities. Even without metabolic abnormalities, obesity was associated with higher risks of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (hazard ratio [HR] 1.46 in men; HR 1.34 in women), heart failure (HR 1.63 in men; HR 1.69 in women), liver disease (HR 2.37 in men; HR 4.44 in women), and all-cause mortality (HR 1.36 in men; HR 1.27 in women). Because this design is observational, it cannot prove causation, and baseline measurements may not reflect metabolic status changes over the follow-up period. Practical meaning: Having a body mass index in the obesity range may carry long-term cardiometabolic risks even if standard metabolic lab markers currently appear normal.
longevity.evidenceNote: Prospective cohort study of 157,159 adults · summary based on the abstract

primaryLinks.title: Obesity, metabolic health status, and adverse outcomes in men and women.

longevity.headline: Menopausal Hormone Therapy Linked to Lower Odds of Alzheimer's Pathology in Two Cohorts
longevity.summary: Because the full abstract is unavailable, this account is based on the published title and linked discussion. In an observational analysis across two US cohorts, women using estrogen therapy reportedly showed approximately 35% lower odds of Alzheimer's disease neuropathology at autopsy alongside fewer clinical dementia diagnoses. Because this is an observational study rather than a randomized trial, it demonstrates an association rather than direct causation, and results may be confounded by healthy-user bias, timing of initiation, or formulation differences. Practical meaning: Estrogen therapy during menopause may be associated with reduced Alzheimer's neuropathology, but decisions about hormone therapy should be individualized with a healthcare provider based on overall risks and benefits.

longevity.headline: Plant Fat Intake Linked to Lower Cardiovascular and Overall Mortality in 24-Year Cohort
longevity.summary: In a prospective cohort study of 407,531 US adults (NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study, mean age 61.2 years) followed for 24 years, researchers evaluated the relationship between specific fat sources and death. Comparing the highest to lowest quintile of intake, higher plant fat consumption—particularly from vegetable oils and grains—was associated with lower overall mortality (hazard ratio [HR] 0.91; 24-year adjusted absolute risk difference [ARD] -1.10%) and lower cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality (HR 0.86; ARD -0.73%). Conversely, higher intake of animal fat was associated with increased mortality (HR 1.16; ARD +0.78% for overall; HR 1.14; ARD +0.32% for CVD). In substitution models, replacing 5% of daily energy from animal fat with plant fat was associated with a 4% to 24% lower overall mortality. Because this was an observational study relying on a single baseline dietary questionnaire, it cannot establish causation and residual confounding remains possible. Practical meaning: Swapping some animal fats for plant-based sources like vegetable oils may help modestly lower long-term mortality and cardiovascular risk.
longevity.evidenceNote: Prospective cohort study of 407,531 adults · summary based on the abstract

primaryLinks.title: Plant and Animal Fat Intake and Overall and Cardiovascular Disease Mortality.

longevity.headline: US Excess Deaths Linked to Cardiometabolic Disease, Substance Use, and Suicide
longevity.summary: Based on linked discussion of a study published in JAMA Network Open (full abstract unavailable), researchers examined drivers of excess mortality in the United States compared with other high-income nations. longevity.headline: Evening light-emitting eReader use delays sleep onset and melatonin release compared to print books
longevity.summary: In a controlled laboratory crossover trial, researchers evaluated the effects of reading on a light-emitting eReader versus a printed book for four hours before bedtime. Compared with reading printed material, using light-emitting screens significantly suppressed the sleep-promoting hormone melatonin, lengthened the time needed to fall asleep, delayed circadian timing, reduced REM sleep, and decreased alertness the following morning. Because this was a tightly controlled experimental trial, it demonstrated direct causal physiological effects of pre-bed screen exposure. The primary limitation is that participants were studied in a strictly controlled inpatient environment, which may not capture real-world variables like ambient lighting or varying screen brightness. Practical meaning: Swapping illuminated screens for printed reading material before bed likely helps preserve natural melatonin release and improves sleep quality.
longevity.evidenceNote: Controlled laboratory crossover trial · summary based on the abstract
